key_insight: Nominally cubic CsGeBr3 hosts long-lived, one-dimensional polar chains despite having zero net polarization.
engineering_relevance: These slow local polarization dynamics could inform models of halide-perovskite behavior, although the study does not establish solar-cell performance benefits.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics using first-principles-trained interatomic potentials.
Analysis of Ge off-centering, polar correlations, and relaxation dynamics.
Investigation of chain-by-chain polarization reversal in the ferroelectric phase.
evidence_signal: Simulations reveal chains extending at least tens of nanometers and relaxing on nanosecond timescales, four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3, with CsSnBr3 intermediate.
watch_item: Experimental confirmation and relevance to operating solar-cell devices remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
